card.name: Subject word inside an if/once clause
card.fires_on: The word right after a conditional or time opener such as "If" or "Once", usually "you", "they" or "are", in web instructions. It also fires on the next word or two of the clause, such as "installed" or "required".

modes.label: Subject after If/Once
modes.description: The pronoun or verb that follows an opening "If" or "Once" in a user instruction.
modes.example: Download InfoIf<< you>> experience problems downloading a file

modes.label: Later in the condition
modes.description: A word further along in a condition about a tool, program or login.
modes.example: Double click the ejs_qm_DoubleSlitWaveParticleDuality.jar file to run the program if Java is<< installed>>.

card.writes: It seems to push toward the end of a condition clause, and away from words like "enough" and "sufficient".
card.plain: It fires inside an "if you..." or "once you..." clause, as in website help text.
